title: 1997 AHSME Problem 3
statement: If \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z\) are real numbers such that \[ \begin{aligned} (x-3)^2+(y-4)^2\\ {}+(z-5)^2&=0, \end{aligned} \] then \(x+y+z=\)

solutions.text: All three squares are nonnegative, so each must be \(0.\) Hence \(x=3,\) \(y=4,\) \(z=5,\) and \(x+y+z=12.\) The correct answer is D.
hints: Each squared real quantity is nonnegative
A sum of nonnegative terms is zero only when every term is zero
